acceptance: The stalling test or fixture is identified, with the evidence recorded, and fixed or skipped on Windows with a stated reason
The Windows fast tier (Python 3.11 and 3.12) completes, pass or fail, in 3 consecutive runs without a stall
context:
Found while checking why 3.11 was cancelled on 2026-10-08. Run 37001178603 (2026-10-02) had a completed Windows 3.11 job, so the hang is intermittent.

2026-10-09 tracker review: retitled and re-scoped. The stall is mid-run at 90-95%, not at teardown; the PyEval_SaveThread fatal error is a side effect of cancellation. The hang list above covers runs 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-09. This item is a need of nightly-v2-windows-unit-leg-20261009. The criterion is not tied to nightly.yml or to Python 3.11, because the new nightly-v2 Windows domain runs Python 3.12 only.

2026-10-13: no stall in nightly.yml run 38318801976 (develop 2bdcb75fd). Windows 3.12 finished its fast tests in 3036.94s (50m37s) and 3.11 in 2605.87s (43m26s), 19 and 20 failures respectively, none a timeout. This is one completed run, so it does not show the hang is fixed; the faulthandler_timeout instrumentation (D-W6) is still needed to catch the next stall.

2026-10-13 later reading of earlier runs: both Windows legs also completed (Run fast tests failed on assertions, job not cancelled) in scheduled runs 38048554571 (2026-10-10, 3.12 about 51 min, 3.11 about 53 min), 38136544803 (2026-10-11, 3.12 about 42 min, 3.11 about 53 min), 38257581119 (2026-10-12, 3.12 about 52 min, 3.11 about 59 min). That is four consecutive nightly.yml runs, eight Windows legs, with no stall; every earlier 3.11 run since 2026-10-05 stalled. Acceptance criterion 2 is therefore met by observed runs, but criterion 1 is not: the stalling test or fixture was never identified and nothing was changed to fix or skip it, so the cause of the earlier stall is unknown (likely changed incidentally). Left open on purpose. Recommendation for the owner: either accept criterion 1 as not reproducible and close with this evidence, or keep the item until one Windows leg stalls again with faulthandler output. No instrumentation PR was opened because there is no failing run to learn from and nightly.yml is being retired.

2026-10-15 takeover closeout: live GitHub job records for all eight Windows fast-test steps in runs 38048554571 (Oct 10), 38136544803 (Oct 11), 38257581119 (Oct 12), and 38318801976 (Oct 13) show completed steps with failure conclusions, not canceled or timed-out steps. Individual durations were 49m43s/51m01s, 40m39s/51m32s, 50m23s/57m05s, and 43m38s/50m52s for Python 3.12/3.11 by run order. The failures were test assertions; none of the eight runs stalled or hit the job timeout. Owner decision: accept criterion 1 as not reproducible and close based on four consecutive complete runs; the original stall cause remains unknown. Future recurrence in nightly-v2 should get faulthandler/per-worker diagnostics.
description:
The Windows fast-test run stalls part-way through. Progress stops mid-run at 90-95% and nothing prints until the job is cancelled. The earlier reading of this as an xdist teardown hang was wrong. The 'Fatal Python error: PyEval_SaveThread ... GIL' message comes from xdist (execnet termkill) tearing workers down during cancellation, so it is a side effect and not the cause.

Evidence:
- Python 3.11 hung in every nightly.yml run since 2026-10-05: 37301643110, 37462397762, 37619200963, 37776283388, 37928417334, 37967682464.
- Python 3.12 hung on 2026-10-03 (37117386123) and 2026-10-07 (37619200963); other 3.12 runs finished (47.7 minutes with coverage in 37967682464).
- --timeout=120 (nightly.yml:71) never fired, so the stalled test is not stuck inside a test that pytest-timeout can interrupt, or the stall is in a fixture, collection or worker-communication step.
- The 90-minute job timeout (#2825) now bounds the stall, so it fails in 90 minutes and not 6 hours.

Lead: enable faulthandler_timeout in the pytest configuration, or run with verbose per-worker output (for example -v with --dist loadfile or -n 0 on a subset), so the stuck test or fixture appears in the log before cancellation. Then fix it, or skip it on Windows with a reason.
